newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai 1997 C/A deficit seen at 6.9 pct of GDP.
newsitem.headline: Thai 1997 C/A deficit seen at 6.9 pct of GDP.

text.p: Thailand's current account deficit is projected to narrow sharply to 6.9 percent of gross domestic product (GDP) this year from 8.2 percent in 1996, a deputy government spokesman said on Monday.

The lower projected deficit, released after a weekly economic cabinet meeting, was a further improvement on an estimate made by central bank governor Rerngchai Marakanond early this month that the 1997 deficit would ease to less than 7.5 percent of GDP.

Spokesman Sunai Julapongsathorn told reporters the cabinet was briefed by the finance ministry, which expects the 1997 trade deficit to widen at a slower three percent from the 1996 level against an 11.7 percent increase in 1996 over 1995.

Sunai said the government expected exports to rise about 10 percent this year after a 0.2 percent contraction in 1996, while it expects imports to increase about seven percent against an estimated 2.3 percent growth last year.
"(The) Thai trade performance should fare better this year due to expected market recovery in ASEAN (Association of South East Asian Nations), Japan and the European Union," he said.

Finance Minister Amnuay Viravan earlier won cabinet approval for a combined 106 billion baht ($4.08 billion) in government and state enterprise budget cuts during the 1996/1997 fiscal year ending September 30.
